title: Discovery: Dedicated capacity discussion with Zenith Bank
header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Laura Chen (Zenith Head of ML), Marcus Okafor (Zenith Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Zenith Security), Tom Riley (Zenith Product)
summary: Discovery call focused on Zenith Bank's requirements for dedicated GPU capacity. Key themes: isolation needs for regulated financial data, burst/backup capacity strategies, expected throughput and latency targets, autoscaling vs reserved guarantees, compliance (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and next steps to run benchmarks and share pricing. SE to scope pilot environment and provide sizing recommendation.
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — this is Ava from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Laura Chen: Hey Ava, Laura here.
[00:07] Marcus Okafor: Marcus on infra.
[00:09] Priya Shah: Priya from security.
[00:11] Tom Riley: Tom, product.
[00:13] Daniel Kim: Daniel, solutions engineer, Redwood.
[00:16] Ava Martinez: Great, thanks. High level we wanted to understand your production plans and then map to hosted vs dedicated vs private. For this call I think we're mostly hearing you leaning dedicated, is that right Laura?
[00:30] Laura Chen: Yeah, for our core credit-lending models we need isolation and also predictable latency under heavy load. We're evaluating dedicated reserved GPUs, and we need to know about burst patterns and plan for peak-of-month traffic.
[00:45] Daniel Kim: Totally. Can you share current QPS and model sizes so we can baseline sizing?
[00:50] Marcus Okafor: Sure, rough numbers: our inference tier does about 300 rps average across endpoints, spikes up to 1200 rps during batch processing windows. Models are 7B and 30B variants, though 30B only for higher-fidelity scoring. Sequence length usually 256 to 512.
[01:12] Daniel Kim: Ok that's useful. For dedicated we typically size by concurrent token throughput and memory footprint. For 30B quantized to nf4 or int8 you can expect X GB KV cache per model — sorry, there's a little bit of transcription shorthand there — but basically a single A100-class GPU can handle roughly Y rps for the 7B and maybe Z for the 30B depending on batching.
[01:35] Marcus Okafor: When you say "burst", do you support bursting into hosted capacity or spot capacity? We can't have data leave our VPC.
[01:42] Ava Martinez: Good question. For Redwood Dedicated we offer reserved pools in your account/tenant. We support burst policies into our reserved pool tiers and optionally into guarded burst nodes that are still in the same private tenancy, not cross-tenant. If you need fully private/on-prem, we have Redwood Private but that changes the ops model.
[01:58] Priya Shah: For compliance we need audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and SSO via SAML. Also data residency: data can't leave our region.
[02:08] Daniel Kim: All of those are supported. Dedicated can be deployed in your VPC with a private control plane, we integrate with KMS and SSO, and we preserve audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 docs.
[02:20] Tom Riley: Curious about failover. If a reserved node goes down during a spike, what's the fallback?
[02:26] Daniel Kim: We support a multi-tier routing policy: primary reserved pool, fallback to lower-tier reserved nodes, then to burst nodes. If you're on a private deployment with strict constraints, fallback options are more limited. We also support canary rollouts and automatic model variant fallback (e.g., 30B -> 7B) to preserve latency at cost of quality.
[02:46] Laura Chen: That model fallback sounds interesting — are quality regressions monitored? We need to tie regressions to eval prompts.
[02:52] Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates quality monitoring; you can upload prompt sets and we alert on regressions and tie them to rollouts. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[03:04] Marcus Okafor: Back to sizing — can you give a concrete example: if we want to guarantee 95th percentile latency under 200ms for the 7B, how many GPUs?
[03:12] Daniel Kim: Quick ballpark: for 7B at 256 tokens and batching tuned for latency we might target 4-6 A100-class GPUs to comfortably hit that SLO given 300 rps average and 1200 spikes. For 30B you'd need more memory and more GPUs; often customers reserve a smaller pool for steady traffic and allow burst nodes for spikes.
[03:30] Priya Shah: What's the isolation model? We need tenant isolation and encrypted in-transit and at-rest with customer keys. We also require audit trails for model access.
[03:38] Daniel Kim: Dedicated provides tenant-level isolation. Data at rest can be encrypted with your KMS; in-transit uses mTLS. Audit logs include token-level metadata and can be shipped to your SIEM.
[03:48] Tom Riley: Any limitations around quantization? Some of our models are sensitive to int8.
[03:52] Daniel Kim: We support multiple quantization profiles. We do recommend testing with your accuracy evals — Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles based on workload and quality budgets. Some models degrade with aggressive quantization so we can run a small eval suite in the pilot.
[04:10] Laura Chen: Pilot — yes. We'd like a pilot that mirrors peak loads for a week. Can Redwood help with benchmarking?
[04:16] Ava Martinez: Absolutely. Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks, include baseline benchmarks on your model and traffic patterns, and we provide a sizing and cost report. We'll need sample prompts, SLOs, and a short list of endpoints.
[04:28] Marcus Okafor: On the ops side, how fast can we scale up reserved GPUs? We have procurement cycles and need predictability.
[04:34] Daniel Kim: For Dedicated reserved, there's a provisioning lead time — usually a few days to a couple weeks depending on capacity in region. We support autoscaling policies within your reserved pool and can pre-warm burst nodes. For strict procurement your account team can negotiate committed capacities.
[04:50] Priya Shah: Does Redwood provide an encryption key bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow for on-prem and cloud?
[04:56] Ava Martinez: Yes, we support BYOK via KMS integrations and HSM for private deployments.
[05:02] Tom Riley: Pricing — is dedicated billed per GPU-hour with a commitment uplift?
[05:07] Ava Martinez: We do usage + reserved commitment. Reserved capacity has monthly/annual commit pricing with discounts. Bursting is priced differently. We'll share a pricing sheet that details per-GPU rates, overage, and burst pricing.
[05:18] Laura Chen: Some of our stakeholders also evaluate Anthropic and AWS Bedrock — have you done comparisons?
[05:23] Ava Martinez: We have performance and cost benchmarks we've run internally; I'll share the deck. Differences typically come down to model catalog, latency and price under production load, and private deployment options.
[05:33] Marcus Okafor: Networking: we require private peering and VPC endpoint support.
[05:37] Daniel Kim: Supported. We'll map the network flows — we can do private endpoints and peering with dedicated tenancy.
[05:42] Priya Shah: Also need details about data retention and ability to opt out of telemetry.
[05:47] Maya Patel: We can provide options to limit telemetry; audit logs are preserved per your retention policy. We'll include details in the security pack.
[05:55] Tom Riley: For burst strategy — do customers typically reserve a baseline and then autoscale within that pool, or keep a small baseline and rely on burst nodes?
[06:03] Daniel Kim: Both patterns exist. Many customers reserve baseline capacity sized for 99th percentile of normal traffic and use burst nodes for rare spikes; others keep smaller baseline to reduce committed cost and accept slightly higher latencies during spikes. We can model cost tradeoffs for you.
[06:18] Laura Chen: We need to present an ops runbook to our SREs — who from Redwood would own onboarding?
[06:24] Ava Martinez: Typically our CSM (Maya) coordinates onboarding and the SE (Daniel) owns benchmarks and runbook content. I'll be the primary AE for contracting.
[06:33] Marcus Okafor: Can Redwood support private deployment in our data center? Latency is critical for some regions.
[06:38] Daniel Kim: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem with air-gapped options. That adds some integration work and different SLAs.
[06:45] Priya Shah: How about compliance evidence — pen tests, SOC2 report?
[06:50] Maya Patel: We'll share SOC2, pen test summaries, and our security questionnaire answers as part of the security pack.
[06:58] Tom Riley: Any gotchas about model pinning and rollouts? If we pin to a model version, do you still push runtime changes?
[07:04] Daniel Kim: You can pin model versions; runtime updates are separate, and we handle compatibility. We'll run regressions against your eval set before any automatic rollout if you've opted into that.
[07:16] Laura Chen: Ok next steps: we want a pilot plan, pricing, security docs, and a runbook for our SREs. Also a recommended sizing doc and cost model.
[07:25] Ava Martinez: Sounds good. We'll scope a 3-week pilot: baseline benchmarks + peak testing, recommended reserved pool sizing, and a cost/throughput report. We'll also include an option for private deployment scoping if you decide to move that direction.
[07:36] Marcus Okafor: Timeline — we have a procurement window in mid-June, so if pilot results are positive we'd like to commit by end of June.
[07:42] Ava Martinez: That aligns. We'll aim to deliver pilot plan and pricing by 2026-05-25.
[07:48] Priya Shah: One more question on RBAC — can we federate roles with our IdP and map to Redwood roles?
[07:53] Daniel Kim: Yes, SAML/SO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC mapping is supported.
[07:58] Tom Riley: Good. If we run a quality eval, what's the turnaround for quantization recommendations?
[08:03] Daniel Kim: Usually 3-5 business days for an initial recommendation once we have a representative eval set and sample model artifacts.
[08:10] Laura Chen: Great. Thanks everyone.
[08:12] Ava Martinez: Thanks, we'll follow up.
[08:15] [wrap-up] Ava Martinez: Recap: Redwood to share pricing, pilot plan, security pack (SOC2, pen test summaries, KMS/BYOK docs), recommended sizing, and onboarding runbook. Customer to share sample prompts, model artifacts, and target SLOs.
[08:30] [end]

Redwood SE: Provide sizing recommendation and benchmark template
Redwood Security: Share SOC2 report, pen test summary, KMS and SSO integration docs
Zenith: Provide sample prompts, representative model artifacts, and target SLOs
